classification.difficultyReason: Read selected and total equal parts from paired fraction models to identify equivalent fractions.

content.prompt: What equivalent fractions are represented by each pair of diagrams?

spec.description: Two equal tall bars side by side, with six and twelve equal horizontal sections.
spec.mathematics: The left bar has five of six parts selected; the right has ten of twelve parts selected. Both show the same portion of an equal whole.
spec.answerVisibility: Selected regions are permanent givens; no fraction values or supplied answers appear in the question figure.

answer.worked:
The left bar has 5 selected parts out of 6 equal parts. The right bar has 10 selected parts out of 12 equal parts. Both show the same portion of the whole.
$$\frac{5}{6}=\frac{10}{12}$$

spec.description: Two equal tall bars side by side, with four and eight equal horizontal sections.
spec.mathematics: The left bar has three of four parts selected; the right has six of eight parts selected. Both show the same portion of an equal whole.
spec.answerVisibility: Selected regions are permanent givens; no fraction values or supplied answers appear in the question figure.

answer.worked:
The left bar has 3 selected parts out of 4 equal parts. The right bar has 6 selected parts out of 8 equal parts. Both show the same portion of the whole.
$$\frac{3}{4}=\frac{6}{8}$$

spec.description: Two equal rectangles stacked vertically. The upper rectangle has five columns and two rows; the lower has two horizontal halves.
spec.mathematics: The upper rectangle has five of ten parts selected; the lower has one of two parts selected. Selected regions occupy the bottom half of both rectangles.
spec.answerVisibility: Selected regions are permanent givens; no fraction values or supplied answers appear in the question figure.

answer.worked:
The upper rectangle has 5 selected parts out of 10 equal parts. The lower rectangle has 1 selected part out of 2 equal parts. Both show half of the whole.
$$\frac{5}{10}=\frac{1}{2}$$

spec.description: Two equal rectangles stacked vertically. The upper rectangle has three columns and five rows; the lower has five horizontal strips.
spec.mathematics: The upper rectangle has six of fifteen parts selected; the lower has two of five parts selected. The bottom two rows are selected in both rectangles.
spec.answerVisibility: Selected regions are permanent givens; no fraction values or supplied answers appear in the question figure.

answer.worked:
The upper rectangle has 6 selected parts out of 15 equal parts. The lower rectangle has 2 selected parts out of 5 equal parts. Both show the same portion of the whole.
$$\frac{6}{15}=\frac{2}{5}$$
